+The most important characterization of a specific memory address range is
+whether it holds regular main memory or I/O devices, or if it is vacant.
+Regular main memory is required to have a number of properties, which are 
+outlined in the following sections. Address regions that do not fit into regular 
+main memory are categorized as I/O; for example, regions that contain device 
+control registers. I/O regions have a much broader range of attributes. 
+Vacant regions are classified as I/O regions. However, they include attributes that 
+specify that access to these regions is not supported. Any attempt to access a 
+vacant region causes an access-fault exception.
